title: The descended scheme is a group scheme
statement:
Let $k\subseteq K$ be a finite separable field extension, let $J_K$ be a scheme
over $K$ with a descent datum over
$\Spec(K)/\Spec(k)$ which is effective with descended scheme $J$, and suppose
that $J_K$ carries a $K$-group scheme structure
whose multiplication, unit and inverse are compatible with the descent datum.
Then $J$ carries a unique $k$-group scheme structure whose
base change to $K$ is the given one.

proof.text: Use exists_commMonObj_of_effective_projection to obtain a commutative monoid structure on V0 and its product/unit point identities.

For each pair of test-scheme base points, the transport is a monoid homomorphism by hμ and hη. MonoidHom.map_inv proves inverse compatibility. Apply the already proved existsUnique_hom_of_isPullback to the inverse morphism, obtaining i0 and its factorization equation.

Use the product/unit identities at the universal point a=id V, with one input a composed with the inverse. Together with the factorization equation, these give both inverse laws after precomposition with qV. Its flat, surjective, quasi-compact base-change properties make it an EffectiveEpi, so cancel qV. Construct GrpObj V0 extending the descended MonObj and use its commutativity to construct CommGrpObj V0. The requested product identity is the previously obtained point identity.
